glosses.notes: Refers to a palace or palace grounds, and it often shows up in phrases like 进宫 or 宫外 in historical settings.

examples.sentence: 导游带大家看这座宫的时候，没有先说里面以前住过谁，而是先让大家看门上面的字和墙的颜色，因为这些地方更能看出它原来的身份。
电视剧拍到她第一次进宫以后，连身边最亲近的人也提醒她，说话做事都不能再像从前那样随便。
老人年轻时在宫外卖过热茶，所以一说起游客还不多的那些年，他总能讲出很多现在看不到的细节。

example_translations.translation: When the guide showed everyone this palace, he did not begin by saying who had once lived inside. Instead, he first pointed out the writing above the gate and the color of the walls, because those parts reveal its original status more clearly.
Once the drama showed her entering the palace for the first time, even the people closest to her reminded her that from then on she could not speak or act as casually as before.

When he was young, the old man sold hot tea outside the palace, so whenever he talks about those years when there were not yet many visitors, he can always share many details people no longer see today.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to the public security authorities or police who handle safety, order, and criminal cases.

examples.sentence: 车站广播刚说完有人把包拿错了，门口值班的公安就先过来问清楚情况，免得大家越找越乱。
社区那条路半夜总有人乱停车，居民反映了几次以后，公安和街道一起去现场看，第二天就把标志重新放好了。
展览开始前，主办方先和公安确认入口安排，因为周末来的人太多，光靠现场志愿者怕照顾不过来。

example_translations.translation: Right after the station broadcast said someone had taken the wrong bag, the public security officer on duty at the entrance came over to clarify the situation first so the search would not grow more chaotic.

People kept parking carelessly on that neighborhood road late at night, so after residents reported it several times, the public security authorities went to inspect the site with the local office and had the signs put back properly the next day.
Before the exhibition opened, the organizers first confirmed the entrance arrangements with public security, because too many people were expected over the weekend for volunteers alone to manage.

glosses.notes: Refers to a construction site or the area where building work is being carried out.

examples.sentence: 地铁口旁边那个工地夜里还亮着灯，不是为了赶进度，而是白天封路太久，很多材料只能等人少的时候再送。
下雨以后，工作人员先把工地门口的泥冲干净，怕来接孩子的家长一不小心就在路边滑倒。
他第一次去工地实习，以为最难的是搬东西，后来才发现真正累的是一直记着哪一块地方暂时不能站人。

example_translations.translation: The construction site beside the subway entrance was still lit at night, not because they were rushing the schedule, but because the road had been blocked too long during the day and a lot of materials could only be delivered when fewer people were around.
After the rain, the staff first washed the mud away from the construction-site entrance because they were afraid parents coming to pick up their children might slip by the roadside.

When he first interned at a construction site, he thought carrying things would be the hardest part. Later he realized the truly tiring part was constantly remembering which areas were temporarily unsafe to stand in.

glosses.notes: 工夫 can mean the time something takes, the effort someone puts in, or the skill they have built up through practice.

examples.sentence: 你别看她台上只讲了十分钟，那十分钟后面花的工夫一点也不少，连每张图什么时候换她都自己试过很多次。
我本来想路过的时候进去坐一会儿，可是前台说老师正在上课，至少还得等半个小时才有工夫出来。
老师傅修这把旧锁的时候动作看着不快，可是真有工夫，拆开又装回去以后，门一下就顺了。

example_translations.translation: Do not be fooled by the fact that she spoke on stage for only ten minutes. A lot of effort went into those ten minutes, and she personally tested many times when each slide should change.
I had originally wanted to stop in for a while when passing by, but the front desk said the teacher was in class and would not have time to come out for at least another half hour.
The old craftsman did not look fast while repairing this old lock, but he had real skill. After taking it apart and putting it back together, the door worked smoothly at once.

glosses.notes: Usually means a formal public announcement or notice, and it can also mean to announce something officially.

examples.sentence: 学校把停课安排写成公告贴在门口以后，连刚到的小朋友也知道今天不用再往楼上跑了。
平台本来只想内部处理，后来因为用户一直追问，还是决定在首页公告这次问题的原因和处理办法。
社区活动改时间以后，工作人员怕老人看不见手机消息，又把公告放大贴在门口的墙上，进出的人一眼就能看到。

example_translations.translation: After the school wrote the class cancellation arrangements into a public announcement and posted it at the entrance, even the children who had just arrived knew they did not need to run upstairs today.
The platform originally wanted to handle it internally, but because users kept asking questions, it finally decided to announce the cause of the problem and the fix on the home page.

After the community event was rescheduled, the staff worried that older residents might not see the phone message, so they enlarged the notice and posted it on the wall by the entrance where everyone coming and going could spot it at a glance.

glosses.notes: A formal verb for supplying people or places with what they need, especially water, food, materials, or energy.

examples.sentence: 山里的服务站平时看着不大，可是一到假期就得提前把水和药都准备好，不然根本供给不了路上突然多出来的人。
天气突然变冷以后，临时食堂开始向夜班工人供给热饭和热水，不然很多人一忙起来直到天亮都顾不上休息。
老厂关了以后，这片地方一度只能靠外面供给材料，所以负责人一直想办法把运输时间压短一点。

example_translations.translation: The service station in the mountains does not look large at ordinary times, but once the holiday season arrives, it has to get water and medicine ready in advance. Otherwise it simply cannot supply the sudden extra people on the road.

After the weather suddenly turned cold, the temporary cafeteria began supplying hot meals and hot water to the night-shift workers, because once many of them got busy, they would go all the way until dawn without even stopping to rest.
After the old factory closed, this area had to rely on outside sources to supply materials for a time, so the person in charge kept trying to shorten the delivery time.

glosses.notes: Can mean a direct physical attack, a technical attack, or a harsh verbal attack in argument and criticism.

examples.sentence: 平台刚升级那晚就有人连续攻击系统，值班的人一边挡一边通知用户别重复提交，怕数据一起乱掉。
老师在比赛以后没有攻击失误最多的队员，而是先把整个安排重新说明了一遍，免得大家只顾着找一个人负责。
演练的时候老师反复提醒大家，要是有人在车站突然攻击别人，先拉开距离再找公安，不要只凭一时冲动往前冲。

example_translations.translation: On the very night the platform was upgraded, people began attacking the system repeatedly. The staff on duty blocked the attempts while telling users not to resubmit things for fear the data would all get scrambled.
After the match, the teacher did not attack the player who had made the most mistakes. Instead, he went through the whole arrangement once more so everyone would not focus only on blaming one person.

During the drill, the teacher repeatedly reminded everyone that if someone suddenly attacked another person at the station, they should first create distance and then seek public security, rather than rush forward on impulse.

glosses.notes: 公开 can describe something as public or open, and it can also mean making information known openly to everyone.

examples.sentence: 这次讨论不是关门决定，而是让老师、家长和学生都公开地把自己的想法说出来，再一起看怎么做更合适。
公司原来不想公开那份调查结果，后来发现外面猜得越来越多，只好把完整数据一次放出来。
他在公开场合向同事道歉以后，大家才觉得这件事真的开始往解决的方向走了。

example_translations.translation: This discussion was not decided behind closed doors. Instead, the teachers, parents, and students were all asked to say their thoughts openly, and only then did everyone look together at what approach was most suitable.
The company originally did not want to make that survey result public, but when it saw outside speculation growing and growing, it had no choice but to release the complete data at once.
Only after he apologized to his colleague in public did everyone feel that the matter had truly begun moving toward resolution.

glosses.notes: Refers to a citizen as a member of society with rights, responsibilities, and a role in public life.

examples.sentence: 老师讲公民责任的时候，没有先读规定，而是先问大家，如果路上有人受伤，你最先应该做什么。
这项服务办得好不好，普通公民在窗口前要排多久最能看出来，所以负责人每周都去现场听意见。
展览最打动人的地方，是它一直提醒大家，公民不是只有出了大事才有责任，平时的小事也一样。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher spoke about civic responsibility, she did not begin by reading rules. Instead, she first asked everyone what they should do first if they saw someone injured on the road.

The clearest way to tell whether this service is run well is how long ordinary citizens have to stand in line at the counter, which is why the person in charge goes to the site every week to hear opinions.
What moved people most about the exhibition was that it kept reminding them that citizens do not have responsibilities only when something major happens; ordinary small matters count too.

glosses.notes: Used for people, works, or ideas that are widely accepted and recognized by most others.

examples.sentence: 这家小店地方不大，却是很多人公认最好吃的一家，所以下雨天门口反而排得比平时更长。
那位老师不是声音最大的人，却是大家公认最会把难题讲得明白的人，所以很多毕业生回来看她都还会带着笔记本。
这条路原来没人注意，后来因为风景好、弯又少，慢慢成了司机公认最好走的一条进山线。

example_translations.translation: This small shop is not large, yet many people widely recognize it as the place with the best-tasting food, which is why the line outside actually gets longer than usual on rainy days.
That teacher is not the loudest person around, yet everyone recognizes her as the one who explains hard problems most clearly, so many graduates still bring notebooks when they come back to see her.

Hardly anyone noticed this road at first, but because the scenery is good and there are fewer bends, it gradually became the route into the mountains that drivers generally recognize as the easiest to take.

glosses.notes: Refers to the real effectiveness of a medicine, method, or measure rather than just how promising it sounds.

examples.sentence: 医生说这种药不是吃一两次就能看出功效，所以他把吃药的时间写在纸上放在桌子上，怕忙起来又忘了。
大家原来以为换灯只是好看，结果新灯一装上，节电的功效很快就从每个月的账单里看出来了。
这套方法看着简单，可是只要坚持一个月，缓解肩膀酸痛的功效比很多人想的还明显。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said the effectiveness of this medicine would not show after only one or two doses, so he wrote the times for taking it on a piece of paper and left it on the table because he was afraid he would forget again when busy.
People originally thought changing the lights was only for looks, but once the new lights were installed, the power-saving effect showed up very quickly in the monthly bills.
This method looks simple, but if you keep it up for a month, its effectiveness in easing shoulder soreness is even clearer than many people expect.

glosses.notes: A 工序 is a work step or process in making, fixing, or preparing something, especially when order matters.

examples.sentence: 这道点心看着普通，其实工序很多，光是先放什么、后放什么，做的人都不能记错。
厂里把最容易出错的工序先写在门口以后，新来的人虽然还不熟，也知道先看哪一步最关键。
修这台旧机器最麻烦的不是缺零件，而是前面那道工序一旦装反，后面半天工夫都得跟着重新来。

example_translations.translation: This pastry looks ordinary, but it actually has many steps. Even just what goes in first and what goes in later cannot be remembered wrongly by the person making it.
After the factory wrote the work step most likely to go wrong near the entrance, even the new arrivals, though still unfamiliar, knew which part to look at first.
The hardest part of repairing this old machine is not missing parts, but that once an earlier step is installed the wrong way, the next half day of work has to be redone along with it.

glosses.notes: Refers to public-interest or charity work done for the good of society rather than private gain.

examples.sentence: 她周末不休息的时候，多半是在帮一个做公益的团队整理捐书名单，因为山区学校常常等着下一批书尽快寄到。
那场演出原来只是小范围活动，后来一听说收入会全拿去做公益，很多没抢到票的人也主动来帮忙维持秩序。
平台把不用的电脑修好再送出去这件事做成长期公益以后，不少企业也愿意把自己换下来的旧设备先留给他们处理。

example_translations.translation: When she does not rest on weekends, she is usually helping a public-welfare team organize the donated-book list, because mountain schools are often waiting for the next batch of books to arrive as soon as possible.

That performance was originally only a small-scale event, but once people heard that all the proceeds would go to public welfare, many who failed to get tickets still volunteered to come help keep order.

After the platform turned repairing unused computers and giving them away into a long-term public-welfare project, quite a few companies also became willing to leave their old replaced equipment for the group to handle first.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to providing a steady flow of goods, materials, or daily necessities to people, shops, or institutions.

examples.sentence: 大雪把进山的路封住以后，医院和超市都在等外面的车，因为要是不能按时供应，后面很多人就会马上着急起来。
这家面包店每天一到傍晚就不再接大单，因为师傅说原料一旦供应不上，第二天早上的质量一定会受影响。
那边一开门来的人就太多，连门口的机器都来不及供应热水，工作人员只好又临时搬来两台。

example_translations.translation: After heavy snow blocked the road into the mountains, the hospital and supermarket were both waiting for the vehicles from outside, because if supplies could not arrive on time, many people would start getting anxious right away.
This bakery stops taking large orders every evening because the baker says that once the ingredients cannot be supplied in time, the quality of the next morning's bread is bound to suffer.
As soon as that place opened its doors, too many people came in. Even the machines at the entrance could not provide hot water quickly enough, so the staff had to move in two more temporarily.

glosses.notes: Used in dates and history to mean A.D. or the Common Era, often in contrast with 公元前.

examples.sentence: 老师讲到公元前和公元后的分法时，没有先让大家背定义，而是拿一条时间线慢慢把几个熟悉的年份连起来。
说明牌上写着这块石头大约来自公元七世纪，可是真正让游客停下来的，还是旁边那张把旧城原样画出来的图。
他以前总记不清书里的年，一听见公元一九一一年这个时间点，才慢慢把课本里前后的事连到一起。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher explained the difference between years before and after the Common Era, she did not make everyone memorize definitions first. Instead, she used a timeline to link several familiar years together step by step.
The sign said this stone probably came from the seventh century A.D., but what really made visitors stop was the picture beside it showing the old city as it once looked.
He used to lose track of the years in the book, but when he heard the time point of 1911 A.D., he slowly began connecting the events before and after it in the textbook.

glosses.notes: Describes something as fair and just, especially when rules, judgment, or treatment do not lean toward one side.

examples.sentence: 大家之所以接受这次结果，不是因为每个人都满意，而是因为整个过程看起来足够公正，该解释的地方也都解释清楚了。
班长最怕别人说他只帮自己人，所以分任务的时候一直特别公正，连跟自己最熟的同学也没有少做一份。
平台后来把评分标准全部放出来，就是想让用户知道这不是临时决定，而是按同一套公正规则处理。

example_translations.translation: People accepted this result not because everyone was satisfied, but because the whole process looked fair enough and every part that needed explanation had been explained clearly.
The class monitor most feared people saying he only helped his own side, so he was especially fair when assigning tasks and did not give even his closest classmates a lighter share.
The platform later released all the scoring criteria because it wanted users to know this was not a temporary decision, but something handled by the same fair set of rules.

glosses.notes: Means the general public as a whole, especially when people are being informed, consulted, or affected together.

examples.sentence: 这项工程刚开始的时候，负责人只顾着对内开会，后来才发现很多问题如果不先向公众说清楚，外面的猜测只会越来越多。
博物馆把修整过程直接开放给公众参观以后，原来觉得这种工作离自己很远的人，也开始愿意停下来认真听讲解。
医院门口那块牌子不是给专家看的，而是给公众看的，所以护士一直强调上面的字必须简单到老人也能立刻看懂。

example_translations.translation: When the project first started, the people in charge were focused only on internal meetings. Later they realized that if many issues were not first explained clearly to the public, outside speculation would only grow.

After the museum opened the restoration process directly to public viewing, even people who had originally felt this kind of work was far removed from them began stopping to listen carefully to the explanations.
The sign at the hospital entrance is not meant for experts but for the public, so the nurses kept insisting that the words on it had to be simple enough for older people to understand immediately.

glosses.notes: A princess in stories, history, or performance, and often the role carries expectations about status and behavior.

examples.sentence: 那个孩子等着出来的时候一直抓着裙子不放，因为她第一次演公主，怕自己一紧张就把要说的话全忘了。
展览里那件公主穿过的衣服其实并不算最贵，老师反而借它说明，真正让人记住那个时候的不是衣服本身，而是背后的决定。
电影没有把公主拍成只会等人救的人，所以很多学生看完以后都说，最喜欢她后来自己做决定的那一段。

example_translations.translation: That child kept clutching her skirt while waiting to come out, because it was her first time playing a princess and she was afraid nerves would make her forget everything she had to say.

The dress once worn by the princess in the exhibition was not actually the most expensive piece. The teacher used it instead to explain that what people really remember about that time is not the clothing itself, but the decision behind it.

The film did not portray the princess as someone who could only wait to be rescued, so many students said after watching it that their favorite part was the scene where she later made the decision herself.

glosses.notes: Can mean making something stronger and more secure, or describing a foundation or structure as already firm and solid.

examples.sentence: 考试刚结束，老师没有急着往下讲新内容，而是先用两节课巩固前面最容易混的几个地方。
工作人员检查以后说，这段墙看着没事，其实下面还不够巩固，所以暂时不能让游客靠得太近。
公司把老用户请回来试新功能，不只是为了听意见，也是想借这个机会巩固已经快淡下来的合作关系。

example_translations.translation: Right after the exam, the teacher did not hurry to move on to new material. Instead, she used two class periods to consolidate the points that students had been mixing up most easily.
After the inspection, the staff said that although this section of wall looked fine, the part underneath was not solid enough yet, so visitors could not be allowed too close for the time being.
The company invited long-time users back to try the new feature not only to hear feedback, but also to use the chance to strengthen a partnership that had been fading.

glosses.notes: Means adding everything up to get a final total or amount.

examples.sentence: 这次活动从报名到结束共计来了三百多人，真正让工作人员意外的，不是人数多，而是很多人一直留到最后才走。
她把这周买材料、租车和临时加印通知的钱都写下来一算，共计比原来算的数只多了一点点，大家这才松了口气。
医院门口那排新座位共计只有二十来个，所以一下雨人一多，后面来的家属还是得站着等很久。

example_translations.translation: From registration to the end, this event drew a total of more than three hundred people. What truly surprised the staff was not the number, but how many stayed until the very end.

She wrote down what had been spent this week on materials, vehicle rental, and extra printed notices and added it all up. The total came out only a little above the number they had first calculated, and only then did everyone relax.
The new row of seats at the hospital entrance totals only about twenty, so once it rains and more people arrive, the family members who come later still have to stand and wait for a long time.

glosses.notes: Refers to a ditch, trench, or narrow channel that carries water along a road, field, or work site.

examples.sentence: 大雨过后，工地外面那条沟一下全是水，门口的人怕晚上看不清，就一直站在旁边提醒路过的人别靠太近。
村里修路的时候故意把两边的沟都挖深一点，不是为了好看，而是怕山上下来的水一下子全冲到路面上。
他小时候总爱在田边那条沟旁边抓小鱼，后来城里住久了，再回去看见那条旧沟，才发现自己记得那么清楚。

example_translations.translation: After the heavy rain, the ditch outside the construction site suddenly became full of water. The people at the entrance were afraid others would not see it clearly at night, so they kept standing nearby to warn passersby not to get too close.

When the village repaired the road, it deliberately dug the ditches on both sides a little deeper, not for appearance, but because they feared the water coming down from the mountain would all rush onto the road surface at once.
As a child, he loved catching small fish beside the ditch by the fields. After living in the city for many years, he only realized how clearly he remembered it when he saw that old ditch again.

glosses.notes: Means constructing or building something, whether it is a model, a storyline, or the way something is formed step by step.

examples.sentence: 老师拿模型讲这座山是怎么一点一点构造出来的，原来听不懂的学生这次终于能把前后顺序连上了。
导演没有把冲突直接摆出来，而是先慢慢构造人物之间的不信任，所以后面那场争论一来，观众一下就被带进去了。
工程师先用木头构造了一个小模型，让大家先看清楚桥是怎么撑住的，再解释真正的桥为什么能用那么久。

example_translations.translation: The teacher used a model to explain how this mountain had been formed little by little, and this time the students who had not understood before were finally able to connect the sequence from beginning to end.

The director did not place the conflict in front of the audience right away. Instead, he slowly constructed the distrust between the characters first, so that once the later argument arrived, viewers were pulled in at once.
The engineer first constructed a small model out of wood so everyone could see clearly how the bridge held itself up, and only then explained why the real bridge could last so long.

glosses.notes: Describes the loneliness of being emotionally alone, cut off, or unable to share what is in your heart.

examples.sentence: 他搬到新城市后的第一个冬天特别孤独，晚上明明很累，却还是会下楼绕一圈，只为了听见街上有人说话。
电影最厉害的地方不是让角色一直哭，而是让观众从他回家以后一句话也不说的样子里看出那种孤独。
她原来以为一个人旅行一定会很孤独，后来发现只要愿意和路上的人慢慢说话，很多地方都会让人觉得很暖和。

example_translations.translation: In his first winter after moving to the new city, he felt intensely lonely. Even when he was clearly tired at night, he would still go downstairs and walk around once just to hear people talking on the street.
The most powerful part of the film was not that it made the character cry all the time, but that it let viewers see that loneliness in the way he said nothing after returning home.

She originally thought traveling alone would definitely feel lonely. Later she found that as long as you are willing to speak slowly with the people you meet on the way, many places will make a person feel a little warmer.

glosses.notes: Specifically means your father's sister, and it often comes up in family memories, visits, and everyday care.

examples.sentence: 姑姑每次来家里都要带东西，她总说不用准备什么，走进门以后还是会把给孩子的水果和书拿出来。
他小时候最怕写作文，常常坐半天一个字也不动，后来还是当老师的姑姑陪他一段一段改，才慢慢不那么害怕了。
奶奶住院那几天，姑姑白天上班、晚上去陪床，家里谁都看得出来她嘴上不说，心里其实比谁都着急。

example_translations.translation: My aunt brings things with her every time she comes to the house. She always says there is no need to prepare anything, yet after walking in she still takes out fruit and books for the children.

When he was little, he was most afraid of writing essays and would often sit for half a day without adding a single word. Later it was his aunt, who was a teacher, who sat with him and revised them paragraph by paragraph until he gradually stopped fearing it so much.

During the days when Grandma was in the hospital, my aunt worked by day and stayed with her at night. Everyone in the family could see that although she said little, she was actually more anxious than anyone.

glosses.notes: Describes classical music, literature, art, or style that carries an older, more established cultural tradition.

examples.sentence: 她原来只听流行的歌，后来陪朋友去了一次音乐会，才发现古典音乐不是想象里那么远，很多地方一听就能记住。
新开的那家书店没有故意把自己装得很古典，只是在灯下、桌子边和大家慢慢说话的时候留了一点安静的味道。
老师讲古典小说的时候，不让学生先背结论，而是先让大家看人物怎么一步一步把关系推到最难的地方。

example_translations.translation: She used to listen only to popular songs. After going to a concert with a friend once, she discovered that classical music was not as distant as she had imagined, and that many parts could be remembered after a single hearing.
The newly opened bookstore did not deliberately dress itself up as classical. It simply left a quiet feeling under the lights, beside the tables, and in the slow way everyone spoke there.

When the teacher explained classical novels, she did not let the students memorize conclusions first. Instead, she first asked everyone to watch how the characters gradually pushed their relationships to the hardest point.
